hyps.why: Raising an already very large learning rate causes divergence and dead ReLU units.
Very small learning rates leave the model under-trained after 243 epochs, so increasing helps.
With a small learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and more under-training.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at high learning rates.
Strong L2 penalty already over-regularizes, and increasing it further collapses the weights and accuracy.
Deeper networks are more unstable at high learning rates.
Wider layers amplify effective step size and make high learning rates more divergent.
Very small batches are noisy, so moving up from them stabilizes training at modest cost in steps.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding width helps more than when already wide.
Extra depth adds capacity when layers are narrow.
